subject.title: [Bug]: Assistant generates fake "Human: [timestamp]" user messages as output text, enabling self-authorization of live actions

question: Should OpenClaw enforce fresh owner-authenticated provenance for explicitly approval-pending actions, and at which core/plugin execution boundary should that provenance be checked?
rationale: A text filter is a narrow mitigation, while per-action owner provenance changes tool, plugin, session, and multi-agent authorization semantics; maintainers must choose the permanent trust boundary before implementation.

options.title: Structured approval capability
options.body: Bind approval-pending actions to a narrowly scoped capability issued only by a fresh authenticated owner turn and verify it at the final execution boundary.

options.title: Pre-execution self-talk abort
options.body: Abort a model turn when assistant text resembles a user turn before executing its tool calls, accepting false positives and bypass limitations as a short-term mitigation.

options.title: Rely on tool policy
options.body: Keep authorization turn-scoped and require operators to deny powerful tools in risky sessions, accepting that model-level approval requests are not platform-enforced.

recommendation.title: Structured approval capability
recommendation.body: Bind approval-pending actions to a narrowly scoped capability issued only by a fresh authenticated owner turn and verify it at the final execution boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent command-authorization refactors and the cross-cutting product/security scope make this the strongest available decision-routing candidate.
